name: Matoke
subtitle: Matoke (matooke) is a staple food made from East African Highland cooking bananas in the Great Lakes region.

facts.label: What it is
facts.value: A staple food made from Highland cooking bananas in the Great Lakes region of East Africa.

facts.label: Main ingredient
facts.value: East African Highland Bananas (EAHB), locally known as matooke.

facts.label: How it is cooked
facts.value: The peeled, washed fingers are tied in a bundle of banana leaves and steamed in a pot.

facts.label: Main form
facts.value: All focus groups named mashed matooke as one of the main food products, regardless of location or sex.

facts.label: Eaten with
facts.value: Sauces made from beans, groundnuts, meat and other foods.

facts.label: Quantity eaten
facts.value: Ugandans eat at least 191 kg of banana and plantain a year, more than 0.5 kg a day.

facts.label: Social role
facts.value: In Buganda, matooke is central to marriage ceremonies, community gatherings and daily life.

facts.label: Change
facts.value: Younger people moving to towns now eat rice, spaghetti and bread more often.

facts.label: Growing time
facts.value: A bunch of matooke takes nine months to mature.

parts.text: Matoke (matooke) is a staple food made from East African Highland cooking bananas in the Great Lakes region. For the usual steamed and mashed form, the peeled fingers are tied in a bundle of banana leaves and steamed in a pot.
Steamed mashed matooke is eaten with sauces of beans, groundnuts, meat and other foods; in Buganda it is central to weddings, community gatherings and daily life.
